newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end down 1.64 pct on political fears.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end down 1.64 pct on political fears.

text.p: Taiwan shares closed sharply lower on Saturday on fears of political uncertainty after Taiwan provincial governor James Soong resigned on Tuesday.
The index ended down 113.59 points, or 1.64 percent, to 6,820.35, off a low of 6,789.34. Turnover was T$36.47 billion.
Soong resigned on Tuesday in a widening constitutional row over plans by the island's exiled Republic of China government to dismantle his administration in the name of efficiency.
The market had no time to react because it closed on Tuesday before news of the resignation was released.
The market was closed Wednesday to Friday for New Year holidays.
The expected political reforms could trigger a serious struggle over political interests, brokers said.
"All the political territories will face new changes, and thus the redistribution of political interests," said Jardine Fleming Securities manager George Hou.

Investors are worried about China's reaction to Soong's news. "China might think the dismantling of the provincial government will lead to Taiwan independence," said National Securities analyst Eric Liu.
China, which has regarded Taiwan as a renegade province, has said it will invade Taiwan if the island seeks independence.
Brokers said they expected political fears to continue.
"Investors will remain concerned over the political side in the first quarter as most do not expect major economic factors to emerge in a light export season," Hou said.
The sharp drop also reflected worries over Tuesday's nine percent hikes in domestic oil product prices, which would increase operational costs, brokers said.

Some electronic shares showed resistance to the fall due to an expected sound outlook, with Primax up by the daily seven percent limit to T$64.5. For next week, a consolidation range of 6,700-6,950 was seen. -- James Peng (5080815)
